challenges.title: Junior doctor hours, on-call duty and the road to 42+4

items.title: Junior doctors: 50-hour limit & excess hours
items.text: Junior doctors (Assistenzärztinnen und -ärzte) may work a maximum of 50 hours a week, and excess hours beyond the statutory maximum (Überzeit) are limited to 140 hours a year — hardly possible to keep track of by hand across many rotations.

items.title: On-call in the hospital or from home?
items.text: On-call duty on site in the hospital counts as full working time, on-call duty from home only as the actual time deployed, including the journey in — every roster must reflect this distinction correctly.

items.title: On the way to 42+4
items.text: Some hospitals — such as University Hospital Zurich — are gradually reducing weekly working time towards a 42+4-hour model: one hour less year by year, with operational safety unchanged.

items.title: Compensating Sunday rest correctly
items.text: For Sunday assignments of more than 5 hours, a 24-hour substitute rest day is due in the preceding or following week (Art. 20 ArG) — hardly possible to keep track of by hand across many wards and rotations.

items.title: The upcoming BGAP in view
items.text: For nursing staff, the Federal Act on Working Conditions in Nursing (BGAP) — the nursing initiative — is not yet in force, but in future provides for a maximum working time of 45 hours, more advance notice in rostering and regulated compensation for on-call duty — if you plan properly today, you will be prepared when it comes into force.

solutions.title: How Klacks takes the load off Swiss hospitals
solutions.subtitle: From on-call planning to 24/7 coverage — everything works together.

items.title: Gap-free 24/7 coverage
items.text: Day, late and night shifts across all wards — Klacks shows every gap immediately and fills it automatically on request.

items.title: Junior doctor hours monitored automatically
items.text: Klacks continuously monitors the 50-hour weekly limit and makes any breach visible immediately — on request, Klacks hard-blocks the breach in automatic planning; with manual planning it stays at a warning. The 140-hour annual limit for excess hours (Überzeit) can be stored as a reference value.

items.title: On-call duty planned separately
items.text: You map on-site on-call duty in the hospital and on-call duty from home separately in Klacks — as distinct, configurable shift or absence types; Klacks does not automatically calculate how differently they count as working time.

items.title: Qualifications & wards
items.text: Every shift is assigned only to suitably qualified staff — per ward, department and role.

items.title: Installed at your site: data stays on your servers
items.text: Klacks runs on your infrastructure. Staff and patient data stays on your servers — with a local AI model, no AI request goes to an external AI provider.

items.title: Klacksy understands your request
items.text: “Fill the internal medicine night shifts for next week” is all it takes — Klacksy starts the planning, Klacks takes qualification and maximum working time into account.

items.title: Night premium documented automatically
items.text: Klacks automatically calculates and documents the night hours that attract a premium under Art. 17b ArG — as the basis for the statutory time credit.

example.title: Junior doctor rotation and on-call duty, one plan
example.text: Klacks keeps the 50-hour limit in view, records the annual limit for excess hours as a reference value, maps on-site and stand-by on-call duty as separate shift types and shows the ward manager early where things are getting tight — including on the way to step models such as 42+4. You can already store a minimum lead time for publishing the roster (e.g. two weeks) today; Klacks uses it to calculate when the plan must be ready — so once the BGAP comes into force for nursing staff, the planning basis is already in place.
